findings.finding: Configuration model exposes exactly the authorized surface: per-selector enabled/disabled and a single bounded template, plus four palette overrides. No output format, color space, alpha, font identity, geometry, text-limit, or renderer-version property exists on RendererConfiguration, so those code-owned values are not user-selectable. Defaults reproduce ADR-009 / BadgeDefinition.V1Default exactly (verified by DefaultConfigurationMapsToTheAdr009Defaults and independently by reading BuildDefaults/ResolveDefinitions).

RendererConfiguration.Validate (invoked unconditionally by PluginConfigurationValidator) rejects null/unknown selectors, duplicate selectors, empty/whitespace templates, templates over BadgeDefinition.MaximumTemplateLength (128), more than one {value} placeholder, malformed non-RRGGBB colors, and text/background pairs below 4.5:1. Messages contain no user template, color value, or secret; only the selector enum name is echoed.

Contrast boundary independently recomputed from the WCAG relative-luminance formula in RgbColor: #767676/#FFFFFF = 4.5422 (accepted), #777777/#FFFFFF = 4.4781 (rejected), #757575/#000000 = 4.5578 (accepted), #747474/#000000 = 4.4929 (rejected). The check is strictly less-than BadgeContrast.MinimumRatio (4.5), so a pair at exactly 4.5:1 is accepted, matching 'below 4.5:1 rejected'. Note: the worker report quoted 4.429 for #747474 with black; the correct value is ~4.493, but the value is still below 4.5 and the test's accept/reject assertions are correct, so this is a report-comment inaccuracy only, not an implementation defect.

ConfigurationSnapshotService.TryReplace still calls PluginConfigurationValidator before activating and swaps neither _current nor _secrets on failure. The new test SnapshotServiceRetainsLastValidRendererConfigurationOnInvalidReplacement confirms the prior public snapshot, its fingerprint, its BadgeDefinitions, and a version-matched Sonarr secret lease all survive an invalid renderer replacement.

PluginConfigurationSnapshot.From now derives ordered BadgeDefinitions (RendererConfigurationResolver.ResolveDefinitions), the effective RenderOutputPolicy (configured palette applied, every other field copied from RenderOutputPolicy.Default), and the renderer configuration fingerprint. The list is a ReadOnlyCollection (Add throws NotSupportedException) and the policy is an init-only immutable object; no secret value is copied (WebhookSecret is reduced to a bool). Existing properties and the From signature remain source-compatible.

The fingerprint is a length-prefixed, unambiguous netstring-style encoding of schema version, definition count, each definition's selector/enabled/template, and the four effective palette colors, hashed with SHA-256 and returned uppercase. The length prefix makes the mapping from logical configuration to hashed bytes injective, so distinct effective configurations cannot collide through field-separator injection. I confirmed empirically with an out-of-tree harness: identical effective configs (absent vs explicit default selector; #ffffff vs #FFFFFF; explicit default color) produce the same 64-hex fingerprint, while a changed enabled selector/template or palette color produces a different one, and rotating Sonarr/Radarr API keys and the webhook secret does not change it.

The fingerprint, snapshot renderer fields, and RendererConfiguration contain no credential, webhook secret, timestamp, or correlation identifier by construction. ADR-005 secret handling (BuildSecrets/TryAcquire/SecretLease) is untouched.

The 21 new unguarded cases (14 facts + two theories with 3 and 4 rows) execute with no Skia runtime. The filtered run reported Passed: 21, Skipped: 0. They cover valid/invalid selectors and templates, both contrast boundary directions, malformed color, palette canonicalization, default-to-ADR-009 mapping, XML round-trip, snapshot immutability/secret exclusion, fingerprint determinism/sensitivity/canonicalization, and last-valid plus private-secret retention. Assertions compare real values rather than mere non-null checks.

The fingerprint is over-sensitive in one direction: a disabled selector's template still contributes, so two configurations that render identically but differ only in an unused disabled-selector template produce different fingerprints. This is defensible for a configuration fingerprint and does not violate any acceptance criterion (which requires sensitivity, not minimality), so it is recorded as an observation, not a required change.

ADR-010's 'Configuration schema/version' is represented as the code-owned RendererConfiguration.CurrentSchemaVersion constant, included in the fingerprint, rather than as a persisted scalar property. The task's explicit acceptance criteria do not require a persisted schema property, and the code-owned constant satisfies the intent that the schema version be non-user-selectable and fingerprinted. Recorded as an observation only.
docs/data-model.md refers to 'RenderRequest.configurationFingerprint' with a lowercase 'c'; the actual property is ConfigurationFingerprint. Documentation-only naming nit with no behavioral impact.
